target_customer: Regional airlines (United Airlines Ventures, Mesa, Air Canada and others place orders and invest)
problem: Short regional flights are costly and emit CO2; an electric or hybrid-electric regional airliner could cut operating cost and emissions on short routes.
business_model: Aircraft manufacturer selling airliners to airlines, financed by venture rounds and customer orders

founders.name: Anders Forslund
education: PhD in aerospace design (institution not stated on the YC page)
founders.background_notes: TechCrunch (July 2021) calls him an aerospace engineer and says Heart spun out of a research project at Chalmers University of Technology in Gothenburg.

competitors.name: Zunum Aero
competitors.what: Hybrid-electric airliners from 9 to 48 seats, first flight targeted 2019
competitors.traction_then: Backed by Boeing HorizonX and JetBlue Technology Ventures; reported financing trouble in January 2019

competitors.name: Eviation
competitors.what: Israeli maker of a nine-passenger all-electric airplane for 100 to 600 mile flights
competitors.traction_then: Cape Air order for a few dozen planes at about 4 million dollars each, first flight targeted 2019

technical_complexity.rationale: A certified electric regional airliner needs battery energy density, certification and large-aircraft design; the company later changed from an all-electric 19-seater to a hybrid-electric design and replaced a composite wing after a structural test.

defensibility.rationale: Certification effort, airline orders and strategic investor relationships are hard to replicate, but the technology was unproven and other startups chased similar planes.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied or bought Heart in the sources found; United and Air Canada became investors and customers.

market_need_then: Regional airlines and investors wanted lower-emission short-haul flights; at founding, rivals such as Zunum and Eviation had backing from airline and aerospace investors.

identity.voice_and_tone: Mission framing: electrify regional air travel with a lower-cost model for aviation

branding.community_and_virality: Press coverage of milestones: first flight of its full-scale demonstrator, relocation and redesigns; no merch or fan community found.

brand_strength.rationale: Wide trade-press coverage and airline backers (United, Air Canada) gave a recognizable name in electric aviation, but no source ties the brand itself to growth.

pivots.why: Per press coverage, the CEO described the ES-30 as an electric airplane the industry can actually use; reported by The Register

pivots.to: Headquarters and development in Los Angeles
pivots.why: Reported relocation with about 75 Swedish roles eliminated; reasons per coverage not verified in detail

outcome_analysis: Heart raised a 2.2 million seed in May 2019, a 35 million Series A with United and Mesa orders in July 2021 and a 107 million Series B in February 2024, backed by climate funds and airlines. Design changes (19-seat electric to hybrid ES-30, then ES-36), layoffs of 72 roles in 2024, a 2025 move to Los Angeles and a wing replacement delay show hard technical and certification challenges, but it flew its demonstrator in 2026 and stays active.
notes: Series B amount, date and investor list come from the YC page headline and search summaries; total raised reported as 144 to 145 million by aggregators. A spring 2025 raise of 40 million appears only on a Wikipedia-style mirror and is unverified. One aggregator names Alumni Ventures as Series B lead, conflicting with other sources. A search summary says Anders and Klara Forslund founded the company, but no opened source confirms Klara as co-founder, so she is not listed. Competitor facts come from search summaries of the cited articles. Education institution for the PhD not found. Layoffs of 72 roles in February 2024 and 75 in April 2025 are from search summaries of FlightGlobal and Tech.eu.
